description: The heaviest thing on most pages and the least described. Every gate here is both an accessibility fix and a ranking fix, because the text that describes an image and the bytes it costs are the two things a machine reader has to go on.

gates.title: Every Image Has An alt Attribute
gates.rule: Each image element carries alt. A decorative image takes alt="", which says it is decorative; there is no third option, and a missing attribute says nothing at all.
gates.fix: Describe the content-bearing images and give the decorative ones an empty alt.

gates.title: alt Describes The Image
gates.rule: alt text names what is in the picture, in 125 characters or fewer. A filename, the word `image`, or a run of keywords all pass a presence check and describe nothing.
gates.fix: Rewrite each one as the sentence you would say to somebody who cannot see it.

gates.title: Every Image Reserves Its Space
gates.rule: Each image sets width and height, or an aspect ratio. An image without dimensions is the single most common cause of layout shift, and layout shift is a ranking input.
gates.fix: Set the intrinsic width and height on each image and let CSS scale it.

gates.title: Raster Images Are Not Oversized
gates.rule: No raster image over 200KB. WebP or AVIF at the same visual quality is typically a third the bytes, and the largest image on a page is usually the largest paint on it too.
gates.fix: Convert the heavy files to WebP or AVIF, or serve them through the framework's image pipeline.

gates.title: Below-The-Fold Images Are Deferred
gates.rule: Images past the first screen carry loading="lazy". Every one of them competes with the hero for the same connection while the reader is looking at the top of the page.
gates.fix: Add loading="lazy" to everything below the fold, and leave the hero eager.

gates.title: The Hero Image Is Not Deferred
gates.rule: The first image in the document is not lazy. Deferring the largest paint delays the metric it is measured by, which is the opposite of what lazy loading is for.
gates.fix: Remove loading="lazy" from the hero and give it fetchpriority="high" or the framework's priority flag.
